name: Hollow Sign Slate

rarity.note: Everyday goods; no Glimmer in it at all.

summary: A palm-sized slate of fired desert clay, strung on a cord, used for signing Hollow Sign where speech won't serve. Every market from Velkash to the Shard Cities sells them; every factor over forty carries one worn smooth. The clay mix matters — cheap slates crumble, good ones take signs that can be read back years later.
origin: Burning Sands; spread north with the Salt Roads (~300 AA)
current_whereabouts: Ubiquitous across Aurelith's markets and caravans.
properties: Good slate holds a signed record that can be re-read like writing — the Edict has never decided if that counts
Standard sign-set covers prices, weights, water-quality, and 'meet me past the third stall'
A slate's wear-pattern identifies its owner as surely as a signature
keepers: Whoever trades. The Mile uses them too — untraceable messages wipe clean.
value_or_danger: A bit or two. A slate with someone else's old signs on it: occasionally priceless.
adventure_hooks: A dead courier's slate bears a sign neither the players nor any Hollow Sign reader recognizes — a private code worth killing for.
The Edict's enforcers raid a market claiming slates are 'writing'; the Well-Sisters' response is a masterclass in polite menace.
